newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris mayor's wife probed over payment - sources.
newsitem.headline: Paris mayor's wife probed over payment - sources.

text.p: A French state prosecutor has opened a probe into suspicions that the wife of Paris mayor Jean Tiberi was paid out of public funds for work she did not perform, justice sources said on Thursday.

The probe is to examine a report written by Xaviere Tiberi to verify her claim that it was produced in return for the sum of 200,000 francs ($40,000) paid her by the elected council of the Essonne region, near Paris.
Justice sources said the probe would not automatically lead to her being placed under formal investigation, a procedure which could lead to her trial but does not indicate guilt.

Mayor Tiberi, who took over City Hall from Jacques Chirac on his election as French president in May 1995, said he fully stood by his wife "all the more since the blows against her are intended for me with a single aim: to destabilise me".

Investigating magistrate Eric Halphen, who is probing the finances of Chirac's Gaullist RPR party, questioned Xaviere Tiberi about the report last July after finding it during a search he carried out at her home.
The search triggered a full-blown scandal after the head of the Paris crime squad, Olivier Foll, ordered his men to refuse to help Halphen in the search.
Halphen went ahead and carried out the search on his own as part of an investigation focusing on allegations of kickbacks to the RPR in connection with Paris housing contracts.
Last month a court suspended Foll for six months, triggering criticism from Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre that the judiciary had gone too far.

Debre was in turn rebuked by the presiding judge of the supreme court this week for questioning a judicial decision. That prompted Debre to insist on Thursday that he had been misrepresented by the media.
